title: Cohort experiment framework for SDK & quickstart adoption
creator: Rachel Park
description:
Goal: establish a repeatable cohort-based experiment framework to increase SDK + quickstart activation and 7-day retention for new developer signups. Hypothesis: targeted, feature-flagged quickstarts plus cohort-tailored onboarding reduces time-to-first-successful-call by 30% and improves 7-day retention by 12% for web and backend SDK users.

Scope: build experiment scaffolding (cohort assignment, tracking, feature flag integration), three pilot quickstarts (JS web, Python backend, Postman/HTTP), instrumentation for key events, and dashboarding + weekly reporting cadence. Cross-functional owners: PM (this ticket), Eng (serving runtime & SDKs), DX (docs + samples), Design (quickstart UX), Data (metric definitions & dashboards).

Decisions & trade-offs: we decided to run lightweight server-side cohort assignment (reduces client complexity) at the cost of a small increase in backend calls. Featureflags will be used instead of shipping separate SDK versions to enable fast rollouts. We will prioritize a minimal set of metrics to avoid analysis paralysis: time_to_first_successful_call, activation_rate_day1, retention_day7, and cost_per_cohort.

Pilot plan: 3-week pilot per cohort, up to 3 concurrent cohorts. Week 0: roll instrumented quickstart and feature flag in staging; Week 1–3: ramp to 10% of new signups for cohort A, evaluate and iterate; Week 4: expand to 25% or rollback.

Monitoring & rollback: dashboards in Looker + real-time signal in Slack channel (#dx-cohorts). Automatic rollback trigger if error_rate > 1.5% or latency regressions exceed 40ms p95.

Open risks: dependency on ENG-4982 (server-side flag infra) and ENG-7621 (sdk telemetry hooks). If ENG delivery slips >2 sprints we will switch to a client-side fallback for cohort selection, accepting duplicate events and extra dedupe work in Data.

Acceptance criteria (high level): see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes: this initiative maps to OKR: Improve DX activation and retention (OKR-2026-Q2-02).

acceptance_criteria: Time to first successful call reduced by >= 25% for pilot cohorts compared to baseline.
Activation rate (day1) increases by >= 10% versus baseline for at least one pilot cohort.
Retention (day7) uplift >= 8% for at least one pilot cohort or clear signal in funnel to iterate.
Experiment infra (cohort assignment + flagging) is reusable for future quickstarts without code changes > 2 weeks.
Dashboards surface cohort-level metrics and alerts; rollback thresholds tested in staging.
